title: Transcript determines protocol output
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$, and take two input pairs $(x,y),(x',y')\in X\times Y$. If the protocol produces the same transcript on both pairs, then its outputs on the two pairs are equal.
hypotheses_covered: A protocol $p$ over input types $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
The transcripts of $p$ on those pairs are equal
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) with outputs in $\alpha$, and let $(x, y)$ and $(x', y')$ be two input
pairs in $X \times Y$. If executing $p$ on $(x, y)$ produces the same syntactic
transcript as executing $p$ on $(x', y')$, then $p$ returns the same output on both
inputs: the value obtained by running $p$ on $(x, y)$ equals the value obtained by
running $p$ on $(x', y')$.
